title: Normal actions use the red danger button style in friend link prompts…
summary: Red buttons mean "this destroys something", but several dialogs used red for their normal, safe next step: **Log in**, **Send request** and **Accept** in friend link prompts, and the save button in two unsaved-changes dialogs. Those buttons now use the theme's main color, and in the unsaved-changes dialogs the **Discard** button gets red text instead, since it's the one that throws work away. Buttons that really are destructive (Delete, Remove friend, End session) should still be red.

links.label: Issue 2033: Normal actions use the red "danger" button style in friend link prompts and unsaved-changes dialogs

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Know what "the theme's main color" looks like
setup.body: Before starting, look at any filled main button in the app (for example a **Save** or **Create** button). That color is the theme's main color. In the default theme it is **not** red. Throughout this plan, "red" means a filled red button like the one used for **Delete** or **End session**.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Signing in uses a code sent by email, so you need an inbox you can check. This first account is **Account A**.

sections.title: Friend link prompts
sections.intro: The pop-ups someone sees after opening a friend link. Their main button used to be red; now it should use the theme's main color.

setup.title: Get a second account ready
setup.body: You need a second account (**Account B**) with a different email address. Open a private/incognito window for Account B so the two accounts don't mix. Don't sign in there yet.

setup.title: Copy Account A's friend link
setup.body: In Account A's window, open your **Profile**, then **Friends**, and choose **Copy your friend link**. Paste it somewhere you can copy it from again (a note or text file). It looks like the preview address with `?addFriend=` and a long ID at the end.

tests.title: Signed out, a friend link shows Log in in the theme's main color
tests.why: This is the case from the meeting where the problem was first spotted.
steps: In the private window (still signed out), paste Account A's friend link into the address bar and open it.
expected: A pop-up says **Sign in to send <name> a friend request.**
**Log in** is a filled button in the theme's main color, not red.
**Close** next to it is a plain button with no fill.

tests.title: Signed in, Send request is in the theme's main color
steps: In the same pop-up, choose **Log in** and sign in as Account B.
If the pop-up doesn't come back after signing in, open Account A's friend link again in the private window.
expected: The pop-up says **Send <name> a friend request?**
**Send request** is in the theme's main color, not red. **Cancel** is plain.
Choosing **Send request** shows **Friend request sent to <name>.**

tests.title: Signed out, a friend-request link shows Log in in the theme's main color
tests.before: Account B has sent Account A a request (previous test).
steps: In Account B's window, open **Profile**, then **Friends**. Under **Sent requests**, choose **Copy link** next to Account A.
Open a second private window (or sign out of a third browser) so you're signed out, and open that link there.
expected: The pop-up says **Sign in to see this friend request.**
**Log in** is in the theme's main color, not red.

tests.title: Signed in, Accept on a friend-request link is in the theme's main color
steps: In Account A's window, paste the friend-request link from the previous test into the address bar and open it.
expected: The pop-up says **<name> wants to be friends.**
**Accept** is in the theme's main color, not red. **Decline** is plain.
Choosing **Accept** shows **You're now friends with <name>.**

tests.title: A prompt with only a Close button shows it in the theme's main color
tests.why: When **Close** is the prompt's only button it used to be red too.
tests.before: Accounts A and B are now friends (previous test).
steps: In Account A's window, open Account A's own friend link.
Close the pop-up. In Account B's window, open Account A's friend link again.
expected: Step 1: the pop-up says **This is your own friend link…** and its only button, **Close**, is in the theme's main color, not red.
Step 2: the pop-up says **You're already friends with <name>.** and **Close** is in the theme's main color, not red.

tests.title: A friend link that matches no account shows Close in the theme's main color
steps: Take Account A's friend link and change only the **last character** of the ID to a different letter or number between `0`–`9` or `a`–`f` (for example, change a final `3` to `4`).
Open the changed link in either window.
expected: The pop-up says **This friend link doesn't match anyone's account…**
**Close** is in the theme's main color, not red.

tests.title: The buttons follow dark theme and Custom Branding
tests.why: The old red was hard-coded and ignored the theme. The issue asks for the main color in light and dark themes and under a Custom Branding.
steps: Switch the app to a dark theme.
Open Account A's own friend link again.
If you have a Custom Branding with its own main color (or after creating one in the next section), apply it and open the link once more.
expected: In dark theme, **Close** uses the dark theme's main color and its text is readable.
Under a Custom Branding, **Close** uses that branding's main color.

sections.title: Unsaved-changes dialogs
sections.intro: Before: the save button was red and **Discard** looked harmless. Now: save uses the theme's main color, Discard has red text (no red fill), and Keep editing / Back stays plain.

tests.title: Custom Branding editor: Save and leave is the main color, Discard changes has red text
steps: Signed in as Account A, open **Your content**, choose **Create**, then **Custom Branding**.
Change something, for example the name.
Close the editor with the **X** button at the top.
expected: A dialog says **You have unsaved changes to this Custom Branding. What would you like to do?**
**Keep editing** is plain.
**Discard changes** has red text and no filled background. Hovering it shows a light gray background.
**Save and leave** is a filled button in the theme's main color, not red.
The three buttons sit on one line (on a computer screen) and look about the same height.

tests.title: Custom Branding editor: the buttons still do the same things
steps: In the dialog from the previous test, choose **Keep editing**. The editor should stay open with your change.
Close with **X** again and choose **Discard changes**.
Create another Custom Branding, change its name to `Button test`, close with **X**, and choose **Save and leave**.
expected: **Keep editing** leaves the editor open with your change.
**Discard changes** closes the editor without saving.
**Save and leave** closes the editor and **Button test** appears under **Branding** in **Your content**.

tests.title: Playlist editor: Add and save is the main color, Discard and save has red text
steps: In **Your content**, choose **Create**, then **Playlist**. Give it a name.
Start adding an item (for example pick a passage) but **don't** choose **Add item**.
Choose the playlist's save button.
expected: A dialog says **You've started adding an item that hasn't been added to the playlist yet…**
**Back** is plain.
**Discard and save** has red text and no filled background.
**Add and save** is in the theme's main color, not red.
Choosing **Add and save** saves the playlist with the item in it.

tests.title: Playlist editor, editing an item: Keep changes and save is the main color
tests.before: You need the playlist from the previous test.
steps: Open the playlist for editing and choose **Edit item** on its item.
Change the item but **don't** choose **Save changes** on it.
Choose the playlist's save button.
expected: A dialog says **You've changed an item but haven't saved those changes yet…**
**Keep changes and save** is in the theme's main color. **Discard and save** has red text.
Choosing **Discard and save** saves the playlist without the item change.

tests.title: Reading plan editor: the same dialog has the same colors
tests.why: The reading plan editor uses the same dialog as the playlist editor, but only shows it when a reading opened with **Edit reading** has unsaved changes.
steps: Open **Reading plans**, and open one of your plans for editing (create one with **Create new plan** if you don't have one; it needs a name and at least one reading).
Choose **Edit reading** on one reading and change it, without saving that reading.
Choose **Save changes** for the plan.
expected: The **Keep changes and save** dialog appears.
**Keep changes and save** is in the theme's main color, **Discard and save** has red text, **Back** is plain.

tests.title: Dark theme: Discard text stays readable
steps: Switch the app to a dark theme.
Open the Custom Branding unsaved-changes dialog again (create, change the name, close with **X**).
expected: **Discard changes** red text is readable on the dark background.
**Save and leave** uses the dark theme's main color and its text is readable.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Truly destructive buttons are still red
tests.why: The issue says Delete, Remove friend and End session use the red style on purpose and must stay red.
steps: In Account A's window, open **Profile**, then **Friends**, and start removing Account B as a friend (stop at the confirmation).
In **Your content**, start deleting the **Button test** Custom Branding or the test playlist (stop at the confirmation, or go ahead to clean up).
expected: The **Remove friend?** confirmation's main button is a filled red button.
The delete confirmation's **Delete** button is a filled red button.

notCovered: The playlist editor's other "You have unsaved changes" dialog (Confirm / Go back / Save & exit), which this pull request doesn't change.
Other languages: no button text changed, only colors.
